summary: Built two encodings of one divisor family (p=1 mod 4, x in a 2-window, r=4x-p, M=px): integer-only nonlinear Int (y,z <= (M^2+M)/r) vs mixed BV64 divisor variable with bvurem/bvudiv divisibility. On 50 (p,x) queries with p<=260, Int-only gave 9 unknowns at 5 s and BV gave 0; both had 0 disagreements with exact divisor enumeration (40 sat, 10 unsat for BV). The solver comparison says nothing about ES itself.
not_done: Only one family and 2 windows per p; no larger p; no third formulation (e.g. pure BV with 128-bit width); no timing beyond the 5 s cap.
next: None for ES; if solver work continues, scale to p<=1000 with the BV encoding only.

summary: Enumerated 974 rational-coefficient quadratic templates (coefficients k/d, |k|<=3, d in {1,2,4}); for 474,825 pairs (P1,P2) solved P3 = nP1P2/(4P1P2-n(P1+P2)) and kept exact polynomial identities (1432 raw). After removing degenerate ones, 10 non-degenerate identities remain: 3 are the classical 2-term family with a term duplicated and integral for n = 2 or 3 mod 4 only; the other 7 have no positive integral value for n<400, and none is integral at any n = 1 mod 24. This is exhaustive enumeration, not a CEGIS loop: the verifier is exact, so no counterexample refinement was needed (substitution disclosed).
not_done: No CEGIS loop (exhaustive enumeration used instead); template class limited to deg<=2 with small coefficients; no rational templates with larger denominators or higher degree.
next: Extend the template class to denominators 8/16 and deg<=3 with the same exact pair-division test, still checking n = 1 mod 24.

summary: Built a rewrite closure (not a full e-graph library) from two verified 2-term seeds for 4/n, applying split rules 1/d=1/(d+1)+1/(d(d+1)) and 1/d=1/(2d)+1/(2d) with merging of equal denominators; equal triples merged by polynomial value. Only 4 distinct 3-term forms are reached, each checked exactly. Their integrality domains (mod 840) cover residues 2 and 3 mod 4 only; no form is integral for any n = 1 mod 4.
not_done: No egg/egglog e-graph; the rewrite set is small (two seed identities, two split rules), so the closure is tiny and the extraction is a scoring of 4 forms.
next: Add the Vieta-type rewrites 1/a+1/b = 1/c+1/d and run the closure to depth 3 with e-graph extraction.

summary: Model: exponent variables of the divisor e of M^2 with global product constraints A (e = -M mod r) and B (f = -M mod r), propagated by generalized arc consistency using prefix/suffix residue-set DPs (no divisor listing; two constraints iterated to fixpoint). Over p<=3000 (211 primes, 120 x-windows each, 25,320 windows) GAC refuted 22,016 windows, every one already by the root residue test (-M attainable mod r), so propagation added no refutations; 3 surviving windows were unsolvable (incomplete). Soundness held: 0 exhaustive solutions were pruned across all windows.
not_done: Did not implement the literal three-variable (valuation-split) model beyond the exponent variables of the two constraints; no larger p or windows; AC not compared with stronger propagation (e.g. singleton AC).
next: None for ES: the root residue test already carries the pruning in this model.

summary: Encoded 'no solution with x<=y<=z<=B' for 13 primes p=1 mod 4 (p<=109) at the tightest too-small box B=B*-1 (B* = exact minimum of max denominator) in two bit-vector encodings (direct 4xyz=p(xy+yz+zx); factored via a divisor e of M^2), bit-blasted by z3 and solved by CaDiCaL 1.9.5 with DRAT logging. All 52 runs (26 box pairs x 2 encodings) agree with ground truth. UNSAT DRAT proofs (unchecked) are 2.0-140 MB for direct vs 0.33-40 MB for factored; the factored encoding has ~3x the clauses but a smaller proof in 8 of 13 cases.
not_done: Proofs not checked with drat-trim; no human-readable lemma extraction from the proofs; only p<=109; no comparison with a non-bit-vector (Int/pseudo-Boolean) encoding.
next: Run drat-trim on the factored UNSAT proof for p=17 and check whether a short refutation exists in the divisor variables.

summary: Premise false: Pass 1 said no Lean project exists, but lean/ES (lakefile.toml pinned to mathlib, toolchain v4.34.1) is in the repo and builds: after mathlib cache get (3.5 min) `lake build` succeeds in 30 s with only standard axioms. End-to-end run: a Python search (untrusted) found C-form certificates CForm n C a for 168 of n in [2,200]; a generated Lean file applying `cform_ES` with `decide` side conditions compiled with 0 errors, and a deliberately false certificate CForm 13 1 3 was rejected by the kernel. Depth document: lean/ES/ES/Basic.lean, Part (a) 'C-form ==> ES': `theorem cform_ES {n C a : ℕ} (h : CForm n C a) : ESProp n` with the explicit triple x = Cuv, y = nCv, z = nCu.
not_done: Build was done in a /tmp copy (lean/ES/.lake not created in the repo); only the C-form family is routed through the kernel, not the other families; no trusted-kernel route for the non-C-form search.
next: Route the Z1177 BV-search certificates (divisor e, y, z) through a Lean statement of the same shape, if such a certificate family is wanted.

summary: Canonical solutions (least x, then least y) of 4/n for n=24k+1, k=1..200, all found; max denominator up to 10^11.9. x_k = 6k+2 except for irregular jumps (e.g. k=5: 33, k=14: 87). Exact nullspace search for linear recurrences with polynomial coefficients (order <=5, degree <=3) on x_k, y_k, z_k found none; the finder was self-tested (recovers 6k+2 and a degree-2 polynomial-coefficient sequence).
not_done: Only the canonical least-x family; no 'large-height' selection beyond the canonical solution; no recurrence search over other orderings (e.g. z-sorted) or over primes.
next: Use the jumps (k where x_k != 6k+2) to ask whether the exceptional n share a residue class or a P(n) condition.

summary: Analysis plus check: tau(M^2)=prod(2a_i+1) <= (2Omega/omega+1)^omega (AM-GM), so enumeration is XP in omega, not FPT in omega alone; the residue DP costs O(r*sum(2a_i+1)), pseudo-polynomial in the modulus r and independent of omega. Over 8,055 ES windows (p<=30000, 5 windows each) DP and enumeration agreed everywhere and the bound held (max ratio 1.000, with equality at omega=1); sum of DP ops 1.03M vs sum tau 0.78M, so neither dominates at these sizes. The premise that omega is the tractable parameter is not supported; the modulus r is.
not_done: No timing benchmark beyond op counts; no invariant-factor analysis of the group (Z/r)^* beyond the residue DP; no FPT lower-bound argument.
next: None for ES; the relevant parameter for residue selection in windows is r = 4x-p.

summary: Built three factor graphs for the same exponent-plus-residue constraints on 480 ES windows (p<=1000, 6 windows each): G1 global factors (primal clique, width k-1, max 4), G2 chain with residue-state variables (width 3), G3 CRT-split chains (width 4). Min-fill DP cost totals were 2.996e4 (G1), 1.54e7 (G2), 1.42e7 (G3): the chain decomposition lowers width but its residue states (domain r) make it 100x-500x costlier (p=97, x=30, k=4: G1 cost 120, G2 cost 177,238).
not_done: Min-fill gives upper bounds only; exact treewidth not computed; no other factor-graph encodings (e.g. carries in base p).
next: None for ES: at window sizes the direct table is the cheapest decomposition.

summary: Implemented MITM divisor counting with gcd strata for non-units (a = (t/g)(b/g)^-1 mod m/g per distinct g=gcd(b,m)). Exact agreement with direct enumeration on 300 random (N<=1e6, m<=1000) and on 6,750 ES windows (p<=20000); total work 1.9e5 vs sum tau(M^2)=5.8e6 (about 30x fewer operations), max work 117 vs max tau 28,125.
not_done: Counts only (no solution reconstruction); no comparison with the residue DP, which is cheaper still for the small ES moduli r = 4x-p.
next: None for ES; for large moduli the MITM is the candidate, to be benchmarked when r is large.

summary: Benchmarked the residue-reachability DP for N=M^2 (p<=3000, m in [50,999], 300 cases) with a Python set, a Python-int bitset (per-bit gather) and numpy gather; all three gave identical sets. The bitset gave no speedup (set 4 ms total, bigint 25 ms, numpy 13 ms), because multiplication by a residue is not a shift; bit-parallel rotation only helps the additive analogue. The reachable sets are small (median |R|/m = 0.09, max 0.99), so this is mainly a small-set benchmark.
not_done: No large-set benchmark (|R| close to m); no C/SIMD bitset implementation.
next: None for ES; bit-parallel gather would need a C implementation with |R|~m to be assessed.

summary: Built the residual-target decision diagram (nodes = distinct accepted tail sets per level; zero-suppressed). Accepted counts agree with direct enumeration (400 random checks); for ES windows p<=1000 with 6 windows, sum DD nodes 1,949 vs sum tau 22,562 (ratio 0.086), and with 200 windows (r<=799) 6,479 vs 902,236. The node count is bounded by k*r by construction, so the compression comes from the small modulus, not from the DD structure.
not_done: Node counts computed by direct construction of the residual-target DAG, not with a ZDD library; only one target per N; no large-r runs.
next: None for ES; DD structure would matter only for moduli much larger than the window size.

summary: Three verified families (n=3 mod 4: two; n=2 mod 4: one), identity checked symbolically (numerator identically 0). Straight-line programs after sympy CSE use 9, 13, 12 multiplication gates vs 13, 14, 13 on the expression tree, and the expanded product has only 4 monomials (naive expanded evaluation 10-14 multiplications). Circuit and expanded sizes are the same order, so there is no compositional gap at these degrees.
not_done: Only three degree-<=3 families; no family of growing degree; no lower bounds.
next: None for ES; a gap could only show up for families whose expansion grows exponentially with depth.
